{"command": "create", "path": "/memories/session/plan.md", "file_text": "# Plan: Multi-instance pantoken scopes

## TL;DR

Today every pantoken theming mechanism is document-global: theme blocks are `:root[data-pantoken-theme]`,
`@property` registrations are document-wide, `color-scheme` is set on `document.documentElement`,
localStorage keys are unnamespaced (`pantoken-theme`), and `broadcastTheme()` blasts postMessage to
*every* `.pantoken-demo__frame` on the page. Two pantoken instances on one page therefore always
fight.

Fix: make the **scope element**, not the document, the unit of theming. Emit theme/scheme/color token
blocks under element-matchable selectors inside an `@layer`, split one-time `@property` registrations
out of the theme sheets, and add a small `@pantoken/scope` runtime that resolves the nearest ancestor
scope, supports explicit manual configuration, and exposes an opt-in hard boundary
(shadow root / iframe) for cases where subtree inheritance is not enough.

## Decisions (agreed)

- **Isolation primitive**: subtree scoping as the default mechanism + documented hard-boundary
  escape hatch (shadow root / iframe). No per-instance `--instui-<id>-*` prefix renaming.
- **Color scheme**: per-subtree `color-scheme` property drives `light-dark()`, plus explicit
  `[data-pantoken-scheme]` forced-override blocks as the compat/force layer.
- **`@property`**: split registrations (`properties.css`, idempotent, load once) from declarations
  (per-theme `*.tokens.css`).
- **Runtime**: new shared package with `resolve`/`createScope`, replacing the docs-local `theme.ts`
  logic; docs, demo tools, scaffold, and canvas-theme-editor all migrate onto it.
- **Scope**: full — emitters + runtime + docs + scaffold + canvas-theme-editor.

## Critical finding: diff-emitted theme blocks break under nesting

`docs/scripts/site-themes.ts` emits non-default themes as **only the tokens that differ** from
rebrand. That is correct when exactly one theme block can ever apply (at `:root`). Under subtree
scoping it is wrong: a `canvas` scope nested inside a `rebrand` scope inherits the *non-differing*
tokens from the enclosing scope's cascade rather than from the canvas defaults — and if the outer
scope is `canvasHighContrast`, the inner `canvas` block leaks high-contrast values.

Therefore theme blocks intended for subtree use must be **complete** (full token set). Keep the diff
mode for the single-`:root` case where size matters; make it an explicit emitter option.

## Phases

### Phase 1 — Emitter: scope-agnostic token sheets

*No dependencies. Parallel with Phase 2.*

1. **Split `@property` from declarations.** In `formats/css/src/to-css.ts` / `emit.ts`, add an
   emission-target option (registrations-only / declarations-only / both) threaded through
   `buildCssFile()`'s existing `properties` vs `sections` split — the structural separation already
   exists, it just always emits both. Publish a new `@pantoken/css/properties.css` export containing
   only `@property` rules, and make each `style.*.css` variant available in a declarations-only form.
   Keep the current combined files as-is for backwards compatibility.
2. **Element-matchable scope selectors.** Change `ToCssOptions.scope` usage so theme variants emit
   under `[data-pantoken-theme="x"]` (matches any element, including `:root`) rather than
   `:root[data-pantoken-theme="x"]`. Wrap theme/scheme/color blocks in `@layer pantoken.theme` so
   ordering is deterministic. Because custom properties inherit, the *nearest ancestor* scope wins by
   DOM proximity — no specificity war.
3. **Complete vs diff theme emission.** Add an option to `themedCss()` / `theme-variants.ts` for
   full-token vs diff-against-default output. Default the multi-scope path to full.
4. **Scheme override blocks.** Add a `darkBranch()` sibling to the existing `lightBranch()` in
   `theme-variants.ts` and emit `[data-pantoken-scheme="light"]` / `[data-pantoken-scheme="dark"]`
   blocks that flatten `light-dark()` to the chosen branch, plus a `color-scheme` declaration on the
   scope element. `light-dark()` is *not* lowered anywhere in the build today, so the native
   per-subtree `color-scheme` path works; the attribute blocks are the forcing layer.
5. **Color plugin parity.** `plugins/pantoken/custom-theme-colors` already ships a `.scoped.css`
   variant that matches `[data-pantoken-color]` on any element. Make that the single emitted form and
   retire the `:root`-only variant, or keep both and document which is which.
6. **Regenerate** `vp run generate` in `formats/css`, update `package.json` `exports` and `files`.

### Phase 2 — New `@pantoken/scope` runtime package

*Parallel with Phase 1. Phases 3+ depend on both.*

Location: `formats/scope` (serialization-adjacent, Node-free, browser-shippable) or
`packages/scope`. Recommend `formats/scope` to mirror `formats/interactions`.

7. **Package skeleton** following the `formats/interactions` conventions: `package.json` with
   `"pantoken": { "key": "scope", "kind": "namespace" }`, `tsconfig.json` extending
   `tsconfig.base.json`, `vite.config.ts` via `extendBase`, `tests/` with happy-dom, 85% coverage
   threshold. Register in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `packages/pantoken/src/index.ts`,
   `packages/flat-pantoken/src/index.ts`, `docs/typedoc.json` entry points.
8. **Core API**:
   - `resolveScope(el)` — walk `el.closest("[data-pantoken-theme],[data-pantoken-scheme],[data-pantoken-color],[data-pantoken-boundary]")`, stopping at a boundary; returns the resolved
     `{ theme, scheme, color, scopeElement, instanceId }`. This is the "auto-detect inheritance"
     requirement.
   - `createScope(el, config)` — the "manual config to avoid collision" requirement. Writes the
     `data-pantoken-*` attributes + `color-scheme`, registers in a per-**document** registry (not
     `window`, so iframes get their own), returns `{ set(), get(), destroy() }`.

## Plan: Multi-instance pantoken scopes

Every theming mechanism today is document-global — theme blocks are `:root[data-pantoken-theme]`, `@property` registrations are document-wide, `color-scheme` is set on `document.documentElement`, storage keys are unnamespaced, and `broadcastTheme()` blasts postMessage to *every* demo frame on the page. Two instances always fight. Fix: make the **scope element**, not the document, the unit of theming — element-matchable selectors in a cascade layer, one-time `@property` registrations split out, plus a `@pantoken/scope` runtime for ancestor resolution, manual config, and opt-in hard boundaries.

**Critical finding:** [docs/scripts/site-themes.ts](docs/scripts/site-themes.ts) emits non-default themes as *only the tokens that differ* from rebrand. That's correct at `:root` but breaks under nesting — a `canvas` scope inside a `canvasHighContrast` scope inherits high-contrast values for every non-differing token. Subtree theme blocks must be **complete**, not diffs.

**Phases**

**1 — Emitter: scope-agnostic sheets** *(parallel with 2)*
1. Split `@property` registrations from declarations via an emission-target option threaded through `buildCssFile()` in [formats/css/src/emit.ts](formats/css/src/emit.ts) — the structural split already exists, it just always emits both. Publish `@pantoken/css/properties.css`.
2. Emit theme variants under `[data-pantoken-theme="x"]` (matches any element) inside `@layer pantoken.theme`. Custom-property inheritance means nearest ancestor wins by DOM proximity — no specificity war.
3. Add full-vs-diff mode to `themedCss()`.
4. Add a `darkBranch()` sibling to `lightBranch()` in [theme-variants.ts](formats/css/src/theme-variants.ts); emit `[data-pantoken-scheme]` forcing blocks + per-scope `color-scheme`. `light-dark()` isn't lowered anywhere in the build, so the native per-subtree path works.
5. Make the element-scoped `custom-theme-colors.scoped.css` the canonical color form.

**2 — New `@pantoken/scope` package** *(parallel with 1)*

**3 — Migrate docs** *(depends on 1–2)*

**5 — Web components + docs**

{"content": "# Scoping: several pantokens on one page

Pantoken used to assume it owned the document. Themes were `:root[data-pantoken-theme="…"]`,
`@property` registrations were global, `color-scheme` was set on `<html>`, storage keys were
unnamespaced, and theme broadcasts swept every iframe on the page. Two pantoken instances on one page
— the docs site and the canvas-theme-editor preview, say — therefore fought, and whichever wrote last
won.

Theming is now a property of a **subtree**, not of the page.

## The contract

Five attributes, defined once in `packages/utils/src/scope.ts` and exposed at the dependency-free
`@pantoken/utils/scope` entry. `@pantoken/css` selects on them; `@pantoken/scope` writes them.

| Attribute                 | Meaning                                                    |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `data-pantoken-theme`     | Roots a theme scope. Matches **any** element, not `:root`. |
| `data-pantoken-scheme`    | Pins the subtree to `light` or `dark`.                     |
| `data-pantoken-color`     | Selects a custom brand color.                              |
| `data-pantoken-boundary`  | Ancestor resolution stops here.                            |
| `data-pantoken-instance`  | Names the owning instance.                                 |

Declarations land in four cascade layers, lowest first:

```css
@layer pantoken.base, pantoken.theme, pantoken.scheme, pantoken.color;
```

The layers only matter when several attributes sit on the *same* element — scheme must beat theme
there. Between different elements, plain inheritance decides: the nearest ancestor that declares a
token wins for its subtree.

## The sheets

Load these two instead of a single `style.*.css` when more than one theme must be active:

- `@pantoken/css/properties.css` — the `@property` registrations. **Load once per document.**
  Registrations are document-global: a second copy silently redefines every token's initial value for
  the whole page. `ensureProperties()` makes a repeat call a no-op.
- `@pantoken/css/scope.css` — a shared base block plus one complete token block per theme.

A single-theme page should keep using `style.lean.css`; it is much smaller.

### Why theme blocks are complete, not diffs

The docs sheet used to emit non-default themes as *only the tokens that differ* from rebrand. That is
correct when exactly one theme block can ever apply. Under subtree scoping it is wrong: a `canvas`
scope nested inside a `canvasHighContrast` scope would inherit high-contrast values for every token
the canvas block omitted.

So `multiScopeCss` partitions tokens by whether they actually vary across the emitted theme set.
Invariant tokens go in the shared base once. **Varying tokens are repeated in full in every theme
block.** A test asserts the blocks declare identical token sets — that parity is the nesting-safety
invariant, and breaking it reintroduces the bug silently.

## Color schemes

`color-scheme` is an inherited CSS property, so it already resolves `light-dark()` per subtree. A
scope sets it directly, which is why a light subtree and a dark subtree can coexist.

`[data-pantoken-scheme]` blocks are the forcing layer on top: they flatten every `light-dark()` token
to the chosen branch, for when a subtree must ignore both the OS preference and any `color-scheme` an
embedding page set.

Set both. The attribute alone only selects the forcing block; the property is what the browser uses.

## The runtime

```ts
import { createScope, resolveScope } from "@pantoken/scope";

// Manual configuration — the way to avoid a collision in the first place.
createScope(appEl, { instanceId: "app", theme: "rebrand", scheme: "dark" });
createScope(previewEl, {
  instanceId: "preview",
  theme: "canvas",
  scheme: "light",
  boundary: true, // nothing outside can theme what is inside
});

// Auto-detection — what is in effect here?
resolveScope(someDescendant); // { theme, scheme, color, instanceId, element, bounded }
```

Each field resolves independently, so a subtree can override the scheme while still inheriting the
theme. Resolution reads the boundary element's own attributes and then stops.

The registry is keyed per **document**, so an iframe gets its own. Storage keys are
`pantoken:<instanceId>:<field>`. Frames opt in with `scope.attachFrame(iframe)` rather than being
found by a document-wide sweep, and messages carry `instanceId` so a receiver can reject another
instance's.

## Rules

- Never read `document.documentElement` to decide what theme or scheme applies. Use `resolveScope` /
  `resolveScheme` from the element you actually care about. That global read is what desynchronises
  two instances.
- Never write a bare `pantoken-theme` storage key. Namespace it by instance.
- Never `querySelectorAll` the whole document for frames to broadcast to. Scope the query to your own
  scope element and skip frames owned by another instance.
- Don't run `applyMinify(css, { flatten: true })` over a scoped sheet. Flattening turns `@property`
  into **unlayered** `:root` declarations, which outrank `@layer pantoken.theme` and break scoping.
- Use a hard boundary (`boundary: true`, a shadow root, or an iframe) when a subtree must be immune
  to its surroundings rather than merely override them.

## Instances in this repo

| Instance               | Owner                                            |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `docs`                 | the VitePress site (`docs/.vitepress/theme`)      |
| `canvas-theme-editor`  | the scaffold app's chrome                        |
| `canvas-theme-editor-preview` | its preview iframe (a boundary)           |

You're right to push, and my earlier framing was misleading. Here are the measured numbers.

## Most of it *is* already shared

Of 2,921 tokens (lean, no icons), only **786 vary across the three themes — 27%**. The other 73% are emitted exactly once, as you'd expect:

| Region | Bytes | Shared? |
|---|---:|---|
| `@property` registrations (729) | 89 KB | once |
| base declarations (invariant tokens) | 144 KB | once |
| 3 × theme blocks (786 tokens each) | 246 KB | per theme |
| 6 × scheme forcing blocks | 87 KB | per theme × scheme |

**Over the wire it's 46 KB gzipped vs 25 KB for a single theme.** I quoted 569 KB vs 284 KB last turn, which was uncompressed and made it sound about twice as bad as it is. Three themes for 1.8× is the actual cost.

## Why the 27% can't be shared

CSS custom properties resolve by **inheritance**, not by lookup. `var(--instui-color-brand)` reads whatever the nearest ancestor declared — there's no indirection layer, no "use theme table X for this subtree." So if two subtrees must see different values, those differing declarations have to physically exist on each subtree's root. There's nowhere else to put them. Adding a `var()` hop (`--instui-color-brand: var(--t-brand)`) just renames the problem; you still need 786 declarations per theme to set `--t-*`.

## My "completeness" rule costs almost nothing

This is the part I got wrong in how I sold it. I presented full-vs-diff blocks as a real size tradeoff. Measured:

- `canvas` differs from `rebrand` in **764 of 786** varying tokens
- `canvasHighContrast` differs in **785 of 786**

So the diff *is* the full set. Emitting complete blocks costs 1–3%, not a meaningful amount. The nesting-safety guarantee is essentially free, and the "diff mode for size" option I floated isn't worth building.

## The one genuinely removable chunk

The scheme forcing blocks — 87 KB, 15% — largely duplicate what `color-scheme` already does. Setting `color-scheme: dark` on a scope element makes every `light-dark()` below it resolve dark natively, and `color-scheme` support is the same browser set as `light-dark()` support.

They earn their keep in exactly one case: a consumer that can add attributes but **can't** set `color-scheme` — which is precisely Canvas RCE, where you only get to put attributes on a content wrapper. That's why I built them, but I made them default-on everywhere, which was wrong.

Worth flagging: this also inflated the docs sheet. [site-themes.css](docs/.vitepress/theme/generated/site-themes.css) is now 2.1 MB / 187 KB gz, and the docs already pin `color-scheme` through `createScope` — so every one of those blocks there is dead weight.
